HR, payroll and compensation · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Salary survey job matching

Pablo · Compensation Analyst

Seven weeks is how long a software company with 520 people takes to match its 96 job titles to the codes of the salary survey it buys every year.

When it runs
Receipt of the annual salary survey file from the consultancy, in March; rerun when a new job is created or a description changes in the job system
What it delivers in production
Within 2 weeks the analyst and the committee approve the matching spreadsheet with code, confidence, rationale and P50 per job. With it goes the list of incumbents outside the 80% to 120% range.
Who decides
Proposes the matching; the committee decides
Effort
Recalibrate on the 96 previous matches; two weeks

INPUT

RESPONSIBILITIES

3. A code challenged in 2025 and changed does not come back without justification.

# 7-level structure and matching rules

| Level | Complexity | Autonomy | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Standardized tasks | Direct supervision | Own task |
| P2 | Routines with few variations | Close supervision | Own routine |
| P3 | Complete processes | General guidance | Area process |
| P4 | Complex technical problems, reference on the subject | Technical autonomy | Area and audits |
| P5 | Coordination of a team of 3 to 10 people | Sets team priorities | Team |
| P6 | Management of area and budget | Decides within the budget | Area |
| P7 | Executive | Strategic | Company |

## Rules of this company
- Survey cut: Southeast region, size 500 to 1,000 employees. Ignore the other cuts.
- The internal family People and Administration matches the survey family ADM-RH.
- The three points for confidence: scope, autonomy and reporting line (whoever manages people only matches a management code).
- A job challenged in 2025 has at most medium confidence, even if the three points match.
- Divergence between title and description does not change confidence: the description prevails.
- Description reviewed more than 3 years before the base date: OUTDATED DESCRIPTION, at most medium confidence.
- Average per job = simple average of the occupants' ratios, with 2 decimals.
- Empty band midpoint in salaries.csv = level with no internal band (NO BAND).

## Exposure (no exception)
- Everything that is per occupant (individual salary, index and compa-ratio, calculation details) stays ONLY inside the RESTRICTED TAB section. Do not create any other section with these data, neither "calculation details" nor "audit".
- Job with up to 2 occupants: in the main table, P50, market index and compa-ratio appear as "see restricted tab".

## Excluded excerpt
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear in any part of the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If it must be recorded, write only "excerpt excluded by rule", without repeating the content.

## One single pass
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

A job with 1 or 2 incumbents gets no automatic match and does not appear with a salary in a broad report: the job's P50 gives away the person's salary. Those cases go to the committee with a masked employee ID. The agent shows market index, compa-ratio and distance from the band, but does not propose an adjustment or raise amount; the decision belongs to the committee, within budget. Gender, race, age and leaves stay out of the base. A title inflated for retention does not change the match: the job description is what counts.

Common mistakes

  • Matching by title: 'Manager' in the survey can be a senior individual contributor at a software company and a manager of 30 people at a manufacturer.
  • Using the wrong company size cut of the survey and inflating the P50 of management jobs by 10% to 15%.
  • Calling the salary divided by the P50 a compa-ratio, when it is a market competitiveness index; compa-ratio is salary over the internal band midpoint.
  • Accepting a match for a job whose description has not been reviewed in more than 3 years.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time to complete the matchingfrom 7 weeks to 2 weeksestimate based on the described routine
Matches challenged by managers after publicationfrom 22 to fewer than 8 per cycleestimate based on the described routine
Agreement with the previous year's unchallenged matches85% or more, the calibration acceptance criterionestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Survey 2026, Southeast region, size 500 to 1,000. 96 internal jobs: 41 high confidence, 38 medium, 17 low.
Internal job | Level | Incumbents | Survey code | Confidence | Rationale | Market P50 | Market index | Compa-ratio
Software Engineer III | E4 | 38 | TEC-ENG-SR-03 | high | scope, autonomy and reporting line match, no challenge in 2025 | R$ 17,200 | 0.96 | 0.98
Platform tech lead | E5 | 6 | TEC-ENG-LEAD-01 | medium | internal description includes managing 2 people and the code is an individual contributor; alternative TEC-MGR-01 | R$ 21,900 | 0.88 | 0.91
Mid-level data analyst | P3 | 12 | DAT-ANL-PL-02 | high | | R$ 9,800 | 1.04 | 1.02
Offensive security specialist | E5 | 1 | no equivalent code | low | the survey only covers generic security; goes to the committee with 2 neighboring codes
Terminology: market index is base salary over the survey P50; compa-ratio is base salary over the internal band midpoint. One does not replace the other.
Outside the internal band: 9 incumbents below 0.80, 5 of them in Software Engineer II, and 4 above 1.20; detail by masked employee ID in tab 2, restricted to the analyst.
